In summary, our research is concerned with
the climatic conditions that prevailed in Keewatin prior to and during the last glacial advance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Keewatin ice sheet was initiated in a cool and dry environment.
the Keewatin area is characterized by a synoptic regime which is favourable for the development of a continental type climate.
the Keewatin ice sheet was not formed in the manner of a continental ice sheet, but that it was a result of a combination of factors, some local, some regional.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Keewatin region is a transitional climatological zone between the Labrador-Ungava region and the more continental regions of the central and western Canadian Arctic.
the Keewatin climate is more sensitive to the position of the 700 mbar surface than the Labrador-Ungava climate.

the mean monthly composite patterns of weather and height anomalies for the selected regimes provide a basis for interpreting palynological data in terms of palaeoclimatic conditions.
